drafts.title: England lead the T20I series 2-1 and can win it at the SCG on Sunday night.
drafts.caption:
England lead the T20I series 2-1 and can win it at the SCG on Sunday night.

Australia are playing the series without their three best-rated T20 bowlers on Fine Margins: Nathan Ellis (6th of 1,133 rated bowlers), Josh Hazlewood (7th) and Pat Cummins (14th). Cummins and Hazlewood were rested ahead of the Tests against New Zealand, and Ellis has a side strain. England rested their best-rated bowler as well: Jofra Archer (22nd), ahead of their Test tour of South Africa.

That leaves Adam Zampa (29th) as the best-rated bowler in either squad, with Adil Rashid (62nd) next. Jamie Overton was 113th before the Gabba, where he took 5-12 and Australia were bowled out for 108, their lowest T20I total at home. In IPL numbers (the same player run through today's IPL against average opposition) he takes a wicket every 18.4 balls, where the IPL average is 19.6.

With the bat, England have four of the six best-rated players in the two squads: Harry Brook (10th of 1,074), Aneurin Donald (23rd), Will Jacks (39th) and Phil Salt (43rd). Australia's best are Tim David (14th) and Mitchell Owen (25th).

The rating is the points of win chance a player adds against an average IPL player, per match for a bowler and per innings for a batter. Each rank comes with a range (Zampa could be anywhere from 17th to 121st), so players close together in a list could swap places.

The fourth T20I starts at 7:15pm in Sydney on 29 November.

Three are in the top 25: Wanindu Hasaranga (20th of 1,133 rated bowlers), Matheesha Pathirana (23rd) and Shimron Hetmyer (24th of 1,074 rated batters). The rating is the points of win chance a player adds against an average IPL player, per match for a bowler and per innings for a batter, on one scale across every league he has played in.

Kolkata Knight Riders paid ₹18 crore for Pathirana at last year's auction. He played one match for them and was released this month. In IPL numbers (the same player run through today's IPL against average opposition) he goes at 8.86 an over, where the IPL average is 9.3.

Among the batters, only Hetmyer and Rahmanullah Gurbaz are in the top 100. Each rank comes with a range (Gurbaz could be anywhere from 13th to 209th), so players close together in a list could swap places. Mahli Beardman hasn't played enough T20 cricket to be rated yet.

drafts.title: The second Test between New Zealand and India starts at Hagley Oval on 27 November. Before Wellington, Tom Lat
drafts.caption:
The second Test between New Zealand and India starts at Hagley Oval on 27 November. Before Wellington, Tom Latham had faced 163 balls from Jasprit Bumrah in Tests and been out to him once, at Bengaluru in 2024. In the first Test at the Basin Reserve he faced four balls from him and was out twice, in the first over of each innings.

His longest go against Bumrah was at Hagley Oval in 2020: 71 balls for 34 runs, and Bumrah didn't get him out.

On Fine Margins' adjusted bowling average Bumrah is 1st of 137 bowlers, at 20.3: runs per wicket once the batters he bowled at, the grounds and the conditions are allowed for. In these two squads Kyle Jamieson (13th) and Matt Henry (21st) come next. Rishabh Pant is the highest-ranked batter in either squad, 8th of 143 on adjusted average, with Yashasvi Jaiswal 14th, Rachin Ravindra 17th and Daryl Mitchell 18th.

The ratings are the ones on fine-margins.com today, and the Wellington Test isn't in them yet.

Best XI is the strongest side a squad can field under IPL rules: a keeper, seven who bat, five who bowl, no more than four overseas. Wins next season is the player's Fine Margins next-season forecast, batting plus bowling for anyone who bowls two overs a match or more, over a 14-match season against an average IPL player.

Purse left is the purse less the salaries reported for the players kept. The 2027 purse hasn't been announced, so last year's ₹125 crore is used until it is.

drafts.title: India won the ODI series in New Zealand 3-1. New Zealand scored 285 more runs.
drafts.caption:
India won the ODI series in New Zealand 3-1. New Zealand scored 285 more runs.

India's first two wins were rain-shortened chases settled by DLS, and the Hamilton game was washed out without a ball bowled. Two games went the full distance. New Zealand won the first by 244 runs, and India won the last by 22 at Bay Oval on 15 November after being bowled out for 209.

Since 2002, two ODI series winners have been outscored by more: England against India in 2011 (by 335 runs) and South Africa in England in 2025 (by 331).

It is New Zealand's first home ODI series defeat since India won 4-1 there in 2019.

Did 3-1 flatter India?

reviews.title: Episode 1 scripts: pick one (POV, storytime, would-you-rather)

items.title: POV: auction day
items.text:
POV: IPL auction day.
You've got twenty-seven crore and the biggest paddle.
Your analyst waves a spreadsheet.
You wave back.
Sold! Confetti! The room goes wild.
Except.
Since 2018, the three dearest buys each year: twenty-six played.
Eight beat an average player.
Everyone else? Nearly four in ten.
Meanwhile, Mohit Sharma cost fifty lakh.
Twenty-seven wickets.
Next year, give the analyst the paddle.

items.title: I spent ₹27 crore on one player
items.text:
I spent twenty-seven crore on one cricketer.
My analyst tried to stop me.
I thought he was waving hello.
The room went mad. Then someone checked.
Since 2018, the three dearest buys each year: twenty-six played.
Eight beat an average player.
Mohit Sharma cost fifty lakh and took twenty-seven wickets.
Turns out you mostly pay for the hype.
My analyst's got the paddle now.
He's bidding base price.

items.title: The star or the bargain bin?
items.text:
Would you rather have the IPL auction's most expensive player, or three cheap ones?
Careful.
Since 2018, the three dearest buys each year: twenty-six played.
Only eight beat an average player.
Everyone else bought? Nearly four in ten did.
And Mohit Sharma cost fifty lakh, then took twenty-seven wickets.
So. The star, or the bargain bin?
Your analyst already knows.
Tell us in the comments.
